A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GENCLUSTER research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices A–B are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original IOI-2025 model evaluations, submission-constrained GENCLUSTER results, baseline comparisons, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports an extended Qwen token-budget curve in Figure 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same generation, behavioral clustering, tournament ranking, and round-robin submission procedures. Validator agreement, representative selection, ranking rules, and the appendix prompts remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six IOI-2025 problems and 39 subtasks. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added; the expanded token-budget range concerns settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The four-model comparison is retained. Table 1 keeps Random, Longest, Cluster-Size, Cluster-Majority, GENCLUSTER(Random-Rep), and GENCLUSTER(Score-Based) as the same comparisons against GENCLUSTER.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes Qwen's reported maximum generation length from 80K to 120K tokens, replacing the developer-recommendation rationale with an architectural-limit explanation. Figure 7 correspondingly extends its evaluated token range. Other principal settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the unchanged comparisons were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends the Qwen maximum-token sensitivity curve beyond v1's 80K endpoint, continuing the previously observed plateau. The representative-selection and ranking ablations, clustering test-size analysis, tournament-round study, and ranking-quality analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 resampling runs for the model comparison and five runs in Figure 3, with K=5000 using a single run. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds higher-token Qwen results continuing the approximately 351-point plateau. Section 6 newly reports approximately 7.3 billion generation tokens and another 7.3 billion ranking tokens. Figures 2–6 and Tables 1–2 retain their results, including GENCLUSTER's 446.75 score and rank 26.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical guarantees or proofs. The existing scoring definitions, clustering-purity definition, and mathematical descriptions of the procedure remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and research contributions retain the claims of first open-weight IOI-2025 gold-level performance, a reproducible GENCLUSTER pipeline, and improved scores with increased test-time compute. The expanded conclusion reiterates these claims.

C2.justification: v1 discusses clustering tradeoffs and ranking limitations within its results. v2 adds a substantive limitations section covering prohibitive compute and infrastructure demands, synthetic tests missing corner cases, noisy judgments influenced by superficial features, and long reasoning traces reflecting confusion rather than correctness. These materially qualify applicability and the interpretation of its selection heuristics.

D1.justification: v2 adds generation and ranking token-cost estimates and a repository pointer accompanying a planned public code release. This improves resource and access documentation, although the release remains prospective. The existing C++17 prompts and most implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds an explicit distinction from prior systems, positioning cluster-level tournament ranking and budget-aware allocation as addressing a methodological gap. The dedicated Qwen Thinking-2507-FP8 reference is removed. Most other bibliography changes are formatting or deduplication.

P1.justification: v2 adds an introductory roadmap and a limitations section, expands the related-work discussion and conclusion, and revises heading and citation styles. Most existing prose, section ordering, and appendix wording are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one-column to two-column layout, with document-wide typography changes and extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Appendix B's table occupies a separate page. Figure 7 also extends the Qwen curve; the other figure and table identities are retained.

improvement.justification: The new limitations section and quantified token costs make resource demands and failure modes substantially clearer. Extending Qwen's token-budget analysis also strengthens the existing saturation finding. These provide a limited overall improvement: the core method and gold-medal evidence remain unchanged, and the code-release statement is still prospective.
